# The Dark That Makes the Stars Visible

## Scripture
*"The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it."* — John 1:5

## Reflection
In late November, the nights grow long and the cold air turns crisp and clear. If you find a dark spot away from city lights, you'll notice something: the darker the sky, the more stars appear. The faint ones—stars you'd never see against the glow of streetlights—suddenly show themselves. Darkness doesn't destroy the starlight; it reveals it.

This is one of creation's quiet sermons. We tend to fear the dark seasons of life—the uncertainty, the waiting, the nights when God seems far off. But the gospel tells us something different. The Light of the World entered the darkness, and the darkness could not overcome it. Not even death could hold Him.

In fact, it was in the darkest hour—the cross and the silent tomb—that God's greatest light broke through. The darkness was not the end of the story; it was the backdrop against which the resurrection shone brightest.

Perhaps you are in a dark season now. The sky may feel empty. But take heart: the same God who hung the stars still shines in the night. Sometimes He lifts the light just enough for us to see how many promises are actually there—waiting to be noticed.

## Prayer
Lord, when the night feels long, help us remember that Your light is not extinguished by the dark. Open our eyes to see Your faithfulness shining in places we never expected. Thank You for the hope that dawns even in the deepest night. Amen.
